newsitem.title: USA: Florida port bond delayed due to Dade Cty changes.
newsitem.headline: Florida port bond delayed due to Dade Cty changes.

text.p: The Florida Ports Financing Commission bond issue that had been scheduled for pricing Monday was delayed due to paperwork problems stemming from Dade County's government changeover, a ports spokeswoman said.
The $211.995 million revenue bond sale has been rescheduled for Dec. 2.

The bond sale is the port commission's first, and will finance expansion projects at 11 Florida deep water seaports. Ports spokeswoman Nancy Leikauf said the Port of Miami is to receive $43 million of the bond proceeds.
The Port of Miami is overseen by Dade County, which recently elected its first mayor, Alex Penelas, since adapting the strong-mayor form of government.

The county "wasn't quite finished with all the resolutions they needed to pass," Leikauf said. "With Penelas coming in and having a change in government structure, it threw off the county commission meeting schedule. It (the delay) is just a reaction to them not having the paperwork done."
